name: Living Web Server optionally serves authorized HTML pages as Markdown and meets then beats Cloudflare Markdown for Agents
asks:
New thing: We want to fie an issue so that our living web server can optionally do this: Automatically convert HTML to Markdown for requests that use content negotiation headers (Accept: text/markdown)

This is something Cloudflare's pro plan does: we want to add a Requirement to Living Web Server to meet-then-beat the relevant parts of Cloudflare's offerings, an I suppose we should add to computer-web-systems-engineering-services-section as a requirement to meet then beat cloudflare, generally. (I don't think we currently have a "break a requirement down into subrequirements so that its fulfillment can be met in chunks, and that's definitely something we will have to do. eventually, so lets start earning toward that too.)

x-provenance.original-words: asks retains exact Leader demand; source notes below are engineering-derived acceptance, not additional Leader quotations

comparison.house-scope: Optional, standards-compliant, explicitly authorized same-URI Markdown projection, independent of a third-party Pro subscription; outperform only on independently measured same-job client value.

quality-gates: Opt-in off by default; source/public-read authorization before every source read and conversion; never use Accept as permission
Weighted RFC 9110 Accept selection, HEAD/OPTIONS and existing HTML/JSON/406 nonregression
Preserve original authorized content, working links, headings, code, sanitized metadata; no fabricated JSON-LD or script execution
Vary Accept, preserve explicit content-signal and access/security/cache policy; never automatically assert ai-train=yes; neutralize invalidated body headers
Bound decompressed source, output and compute to independently governed host budget; fail closed on sensitive/unsupported representations
Independent agent and second lawful application receiving; prove MEET before any specific real-world BEAT; no self-reported revenue
x-provenance.decomposition-contract: Current emsenn/schema/requirement has no first-class parent/subrequirement relation; these acceptance cells are independent present-schema slices, not installed linked child Requirements. See https://github.com/561-group/requirements-management-team/issues/1
x-provenance.status-boundary: Source-authored Requirement only: no active converter, package deployment, installed acceptance or customer proof is claimed.
